title: Personal Pronouns
description: Subject pronouns used to replace specific nouns (e.g., I, you, he, she, it, we, they).

title: Definite Articles
description: Words used before nouns to indicate specific items (e.g., the, le/la, il/la, der/die/das).

title: Indefinite Articles
description: Words used before nouns to specify non-specific items (e.g., a/an, un/une, ein/eine).

title: Grammatical Noun Gender
description: Classification of nouns into masculine, feminine, or neuter categories affecting agreement.

title: Noun Plural Formation
description: Morphological or syntactic mechanisms to mark plural quantity on nouns.

title: Present Tense Copula (To Be)
description: Overt present tense copular verb used to link subjects with predicates or identities.

title: Possession Verb (To Have)
description: Dedicated verb expressively denoting possession (e.g., have, avoir, avere, tener, haben).

title: Basic Clause Negation
description: Particles, adverbs, or affixes used to negate main clauses (e.g., not, ne...pas, non, не, не/μή).

title: Yes/No Polar Questions
description: Structures or rising intonation patterns used to formulate closed questions.

title: Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) Word Order
description: Dominant default word order where the verb appears between subject and object.

title: Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) Word Order
description: Dominant default word order where the verb concludes the clause after subject and object.

title: Possessive Adjectives & Determiners
description: Forms indicating ownership modifying nouns (e.g., my/your, mon/ma, мой, il mio).

title: Demonstrative Determiners
description: Words pointing to specific items relative to speaker location (e.g., this/that, ce/cette, этот/тот).

title: Noun Case Declension
description: Inflection of nouns to mark syntactic relationships like subject, direct object, or location.

title: Adjective Agreement
description: Adjectives changing form to match gender, number, or case of the modified noun.

title: Verb Inflection for Person & Number
description: Verbs changing endings or forms based on grammatical person (1st, 2nd, 3rd) and number.

title: Accusative Direct Object Marking
description: Explicit morphological case marking or prepositional marking for direct objects.

title: Vowel Harmony in Suffixation
description: Phonological rule dictating suffix vowel fronting or backing based on root vowels.

title: Initial Consonant Mutations
description: Sound changes at the beginning of words triggered by preceding grammatical particles or words.

title: Agglutinative Suffix Chains
description: Building complex meanings by appending distinct, single-function suffixes to root words.

title: Demonstrative Pronouns
description: Pronouns functioning independently to replace and point to specific entities (this, that, ceci, cela, это, αυτό).

title: Three-Way Spatial Demonstratives
description: Spatial distance system contrasting near speaker, near listener, and far from both (este/ese/aquel, esto/isso/aquilo).

title: Genitive Noun Possession
description: Marking the possessor noun directly with a genitive case ending or possessive affix.

title: Prepositional Possession Construction
description: Expressing ownership using prepositions before the possessor noun (e.g., of, de, di, da).

title: Possessive Noun Suffixes
description: Attaching personal possessive suffixes directly to the possessed noun stem (e.g., -ым/-ем, -ы/-е).

title: Dative / Locative Existential Possession
description: Expressing 'X has Y' using a dative or locative possessor coupled with an existential copula ('у меня есть').

title: Postnominal Adjective Placement
description: Positioning modifying descriptive adjectives immediately after the noun by default.

title: Prenominal Adjective Placement
description: Positioning modifying descriptive adjectives before the noun by default.

title: Uninflected Predicative Adjectives
description: Adjectives remaining invariant in form when functioning as predicate complements following copulas.

title: Adverbial Derivational Suffixes
description: Forming adverbs systematically from adjective roots using dedicated suffixes (-ly, -ment, -mente, -o, -ως).

title: Flexible Adverb Placement
description: Permitting adverbs variable placement at sentence start, middle, or end without altering clause syntax.

title: Flat Adverbs (Uninflected Adjective Form)
description: Using the base uninflected adjective stem directly as an adverb without derivation suffixes.

title: Basic Cardinal Numerals (1-10)
description: Core counting numbers utilized for quantity identification and basic counting.

title: Numeral-Noun Gender & Case Agreement
description: Cardinal numbers changing inflection to match the gender, number, or case of the accompanying noun.

title: Singular Noun Form Following Numerals
description: Rule requiring nouns modified by cardinal numbers greater than 1 to remain in the grammatical singular.

title: Ordinal Numeral Suffixation
description: Derivation of sequential order numbers (1st, 2nd, 3rd) using dedicated ordinal affixes or suffixes.

title: Interrogative Question Words
description: Interrogative pronouns and adverbs used for open information questions (who, what, where, when, why).

title: Subject-Verb Inversion in Interrogatives
description: Inverting default subject and verb positions to mark question clauses.

title: Interrogative Clitic / Particle
description: Dedicated grammatical particle appended to clauses to signal yes/no polar questions (-мы/-ме, -ши, ли).

title: Negative Concord (Double Negation)
description: Grammatical requirement combining main verb negation particles with negative pronouns/adverbs.

title: Bound Verbal Negation Affixes
description: Incorporating negative markers directly into the verbal morphological stem as bound prefixes or suffixes.

title: Discontinuous Split Negation Markers
description: Clause negation utilizing two separated surrounding markers (ne...pas, ne...ket).

title: Locative / Spatial Case Marking
description: Expressing spatial location (in, at, on) via noun case endings or postpositions rather than prepositions.

title: Dative Case for Indirect Objects
description: Noun case inflection designating the recipient or indirect object complement of verbs.

title: Instrumental / Comitative Case Suffixes
description: Morphological case suffix marking the instrument, tool, or accompaniment ('with X').

title: Genitive Case for Quantities & Absence
description: Employing genitive case endings on nouns following numerical quantifiers or negated verbs.

title: Basic Spatial Prepositions
description: Preposed adpositions indicating spatial orientation (in, on, at, under, behind, in front of).

title: Spatial & Temporal Postpositions
description: Adpositional elements positioned immediately following the noun phrase rather than preceding it.

title: Preposition-Article Contraction
description: Mandatory phonetic fusion of prepositions with definite articles into single contracted words (du, au, della, im).

title: Verb-Second (V2) Word Order
description: Syntactic constraint placing the finite verb in the second constituent position in main declarative clauses.

title: Pragmatically Flexible Word Order
description: Highly inflected syntax permitting SVO, SOV, VSO permutations for pragmatic focus and topicalization.

title: Verb-Subject-Object (VSO) Word Order
description: Syntax placing the finite verb at the head of declarative sentences before subject and object.

title: Coordinating Conjunctions (And, But, Or)
description: Core grammatical connectives linking words, phrases, or independent clauses of equal syntactic status.

title: Basic Subordinating Conjunctions (Because, If, That)
description: Connectives introducing dependent clauses establishing causal, conditional, or nominal relationships.

title: Present Continuous / Progressive Aspect
description: Grammatical constructions marking ongoing actions occurring at the time of utterance.

title: Periphrastic Near Future (Going To)
description: Using motion or auxiliary verbs ('go') combined with infinitives to convey prospective future actions.

title: Calendar Units & Basic Temporal Adverbs
description: Fundamental expressions for schedule management (days of week, months, today, tomorrow, yesterday).

title: Comparative Degree of Adjectives
description: Morphological suffixes or degree adverbs used to express greater intensity or comparison between entities.

title: Superlative Degree of Adjectives
description: Grammatical forms indicating the highest relative degree of a property within a group.

title: Relative Clauses with Relative Pronouns
description: Subordinate clauses embedded to modify noun heads introduced by relative pronouns (who, which, that, qui, который).

title: Subordinate Clause Word Order Alteration
description: Clause syntax changing significantly inside dependent subordinate clauses (e.g., verb-final placement).

title: Reflexive Verbs & Pronouns
description: Constructions where the action of the verb reflects directly back onto the grammatical subject.

title: Reflexive Passive / Middle Voice
description: Employing reflexive or middle voice morphology to express impersonal or passive meanings.
